key_insight: SqueezeBench turns benchmark saturation into continued progress by requiring each accepted solution to produce a provably stronger mathematical bound than the current record.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical evaluation protocol for theorem-proving models that measures certified reasoning progress even after standard benchmarks stop being informative.
method: Each problem defines an integer function f(n) known only at small n, with Lean-verified lower and upper record functions maintained over n.
A submission must prove its proposed bound is valid, no worse than the current record everywhere, and strictly better at least one n.
Accepted records become the new target, while automated dual-kernel Lean checking verifies proofs and blocks trivial exhaustive-search solutions.
evidence_signal: The authors released 10 extremal-combinatorics problems, obtained 20 initial records, and report 82 accepted submissions from a frontier LLM baseline plus 60 more from newer models, improving nearly all records.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on formally checked bounds and maintainers only inspect for exhaustive search at larger n, it may still be sensitive to implementation details of the admission process and record design.
paper_title: SqueezeBench: Saturation-Resilient Evaluation of Mathematical Capability
